rationale:
Evidence: all 60 development trials ended off track with zero completions. Scores were flat at about 39.85 for iterations 0, 1 and 5, which differed in kp, ki and base_speed. Iteration 2 (kp 4.0, wider spacing, larger kd and ki) scored 26.37, so under-steering hurt. Every raced design shows the same early pattern: exactly 2 line-loss events (1 for iteration 2), max_error 0.061 to 0.067, and progress 0.04 to 0.17. The failure is therefore early and set by something no raced gain or speed has changed.

Critique handling. (1) Attribution: I accept that this revision changes several variables at once. I keep it anyway because the 5-sensor, kp 5, kd 0.02 family has already produced a flat score, so single-change tests inside that family are unlikely to move the result. The falsifiable targets below are the attribution mechanism for this race. (2) Footprint: I accept the correction. A 0.012 m sensor at x = 0.03 m reads tape only when the robot is displaced by about 0.017 m or more. The 0.010 m spacing does give overlapping footprints, so the sampling is denser, but I no longer claim the outer sensors cover the tape when centred. (3) Units: I accept that base_speed is a dimensionless demand. The 1.5 figure is only a rough target, and completion is a risk, not an expectation. (4) Saturation: I accept that the 7-sensor weights of plus or minus 1 rarely reach the saturation signal of about 0.65, so saturation is not a practical limit here. (5) Motor mismatch: I note the offset is about mismatch/kp. It is small at kp 4.5 and I do not change it in this race. (6) I reject reverting to the 5-sensor layout now. Its score is already known to be flat, and a revert would spend an iteration without new information.

Changes from the raced baseline: 7 sensors at 0.010 m spacing (x from -0.03 to 0.03), sensor_size 0.012, kp 4.5, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.5. ki stays 0, line_loss stays last_direction, and wheel_track 0.12 and mass 0.8 are unchanged.

Expectation: I predict a score near or modestly above 40, with progress above 0.3 if the start transient is less severe with denser sampling. I do not expect completion.

Falsifiable targets: max_error below 0.06 on the oval and s-bend; line_loss_events at or below 1; steering_oscillation below 0.16; progress above 0.5 on all tracks. If max_error stays at 0.06 or above and progress is unchanged, the cause is not controller gain or sensor layout, and the next iteration should look for an early divergence (start heading or mismatch) rather than tuning. If steering_oscillation exceeds 0.18, kd or kp is too high. If completion_time is above 3 s with no line losses, base_speed must rise.
